exposure: particles with an aerodynamic diameter ≤1.0 μm (PM(1))
cohort: 59,754 children between the ages of 2 and 17 in seven Chinese cities
finding: Children delivered via caesarean section had significantly higher odds ratios for asthma and asthma-related symptoms per interquartile range increase of air pollutants compared to children delivered vaginally.
mod_finding: Delivery via c-section may increase the risks of air pollution on asthma and its symptoms in Chinese children.
